question:
A 64-year-old male presents to the emergency department with six days of abdominal pain and black
stools. He reports consuming 11 beers daily but stopped drinking five days ago due to the abdominal
pain. He has a history of peptic ulcer disease but does not take his prescribed omeprazole. His
temperature is 37.2 ºC (99.0 ºF), pulse is 96/min, blood pressure is 112/84 mmHg, and oxygen
saturation is 100% on room air. Physical examination reveals normal mentation, no asterixis, and mild
tenderness in the epigastric and right upper quadrant regions. Digital rectal examination shows black
stool without hematochezia. Laboratory findings include a hemoglobin level of 11.1 g/dL, AST of 175
U/L, and ALT of 90 U/L. The calculated Maddrey discriminant function is 39. What is the most
appropriate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) Start IV fluids and monitor for variceal
bleeding (B) Start oral pentoxifylline (C) Calculate MELD score (D) Start IV lorazepam (E) Perform
upper endoscopy immediately (F) Administer IV vitamin K (G) Start IV octreotide (H) Administer oral
N-acetylcysteine (I) Start oral prednisolone (J) Transfer to a liver transplant center
 A. Start IV lorazepam
B. Start IV octreotide
C. Start oral pentoxifylline
D. Calculate MELD score
E. Administer oral N-acetylcysteine
F. Transfer to a liver transplant center
G. Perform upper endoscopy immediately
H. Start oral prednisolone
I. Administer IV vitamin K
J. Start IV fluids and monitor for variceal bleeding
